s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic ankle pain and swelling with bony lesion
salient_findings: Pain and swelling around the right ankle for 1 year
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
key_facts: 13-year-old boy
1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle
Gradually increasing in size
Bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
Ankle and subtalar joints have a full range of motion
Complete blood count within normal limits
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
Submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin

shortlist.label: Brodie's abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Submetaphyseal lytic lesion with sclerotic margin and chronic ankle pain

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pain and swelling with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bony thickening and nocturnal pain are common features

shortlist.label: Chondroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion in the epiphysis or apophysis with chronic pain

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lytic lesion with well-defined margins and chronic pain

raw.rationale: The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin, along with elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and localized pain and swelling, is consistent with Brodie's abscess, a type of chronic osteomyelitis.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: While osteomyelitis is a broader category that includes Brodie's abscess, the specific findings point more directly to Brodie's abscess as the most precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoid osteoma typically presents with nocturnal pain that is relieved by NSAIDs, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Chondroblastoma
rejected.why: Chondroblastoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the epiphyses of long bones, which does not match the submetaphyseal location described.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumor usually occurs in adults after epiphyseal closure and is located in the epiphyses, which does not fit the patient's age and the lesion's location.
